metadata.explanation: Chains image insertion with a font-size change on the 'Figure 1' caption. Getter checks inline image count (should be >=2) and the font size of the paragraph starting with 'Figure 1' (originally 9pt, should be changed to 12pt). Partial credit: 0.5 for image, 0.5 for caption font size. Initial state fails both checks (1 image, 9pt).

scoring_breakdown.image_inserted: 0.5 - Document has at least 2 inline images

llm_judge_reasons: Both instruction requirements are covered: image insertion check (inline_shapes >= 2) and Figure 1 caption font size check (12pt), each contributing 0.5 partial credit.
The image count check correctly compares against min_image_count=2, reflecting the expected state after inserting one more image into a document that already has one.
The EMU-to-pt conversion (font.size / 12700) is correct (1pt = 12700 EMU), and the expected value of 12pt matches the instruction.
The metric correctly handles the 'rule' expected type: it accesses expected.get('min_image_count') and expected.get('caption_font_size_pt') directly without the 'rules' anti-pattern.
Postconfig issues Ctrl+S before evaluation, ensuring the docx file on disk is up-to-date when the getter reads it.

Minor risk: font size getter returns None if LibreOffice stores the size change at paragraph-style level rather than at the run level; in that case caption_font_size_pt would be None and the 0.5 credit would be incorrectly withheld even on a correct submission. In practice LibreOffice Writer sets explicit run-level sizes via toolbar changes, so this risk is low.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: To make font size extraction more robust, also check paragraph-level font size via the paragraph's style or paragraph format if no run has an explicit font.size. For example: fall back to para.style.font.size or iterate all runs and check both run-level and style-inherited sizes.
